## ETF API contract published for TC

- Authenticated route: `POST /api/v1/etf-holdings/{symbol}/acquire`.
- Request `ETFProfileAcquireRequest`: required UUID `request_id`, boolean
  `refresh`. `refresh=false` is cache-only and does not create a missing
  profile. The explicit action must send `refresh=true` to attempt the selected
  issuer route. A request ID is a correlation key; it does not promise request
  deduplication.
- Response `ETFProfileAcquireOut`: `request_id`, `outcome` (`cached`,
  `no_data`, `acquired`, `held`, `failed`), `refresh`, `refresh_attempted`,
  `refresh_succeeded`, `profile`, nullable `snapshot` and `capability`,
  nullable `source_provider`/`source_operation`, `provider_request_log_ids`,
  and nullable `message`. `ETFHoldingsSnapshotOut` exposes its row list as
  `snapshot.holdings` (not `snapshot.rows`). Provider status envelopes remain
  separate from this ETF outcome enum. This matches the TC mocked v1 consumer
  contract in `/home/m920q/charting-platform/.ai/staging-attempts/on-demand-wire-design-review-20261027.json`.
- Unknown, ambiguous, inactive, synthetic, provisional, or non-fund identities
  are denied before profile creation/source work. An existing active, resolved

## VanEck/OIH initial issuer-qualification component — 2026-10-27

This is a bounded local source candidate on published baseline
`b9939d13928749765319475d77fe754102c33e6a`. It adds one administrator-only,
one-shot OIH qualification operation and an issuer-specific adapter method.
The current ETF consumer requires the Provider-owned context manager with this
exact reviewed interface:

`bind_vaneck_initial_etf_qualification(*, job_id: int, fund_profile_id: int, instrument_id: int, provider_symbol: str, account_scope: str, review_revision: int, expires_at: aware_datetime)`.

It resolves that binder dynamically and fails closed before creating a job if
the helper is absent. No Provider sibling code is copied or imported. Until the
helper is present in exact green Provider staging and adopted through Root's
release, this component cannot make an admitted request. The separate job is
restricted to canonical OIH, its curated `oil-services-etf-oih` slug, the
`ETF_HOLDINGS` capability and `fetch_etf_holdings_latest` operation. It keeps
the ordinary policy disabled and entitlement `not_run` on every nonpositive
result. It uses the current reviewed application limits: concurrency 1, at
least 30 seconds between physical requests, burst 1, at most 3 physical
requests, 120 seconds total, 5 MiB cumulative body, and zero retries. Redirects
are not followed; the Location is retained for review. The shared Provider
transport/admission and settlement path is still mandatory.

Before positive finalization, the service locks and refreshes the persisted job,
active DataSource, disabled policy and entitlement with `FOR UPDATE` plus
`populate_existing`. It compares the persisted job scope, entitlement revision
and `not_run` state, source review fingerprint and current account binding to
the committed scope. A mid-fetch review change rejects qualification instead
of overwriting its revision. Mocked tests cover this concurrency boundary.

Qualification also requires body-level OIH identity and a valid composition
date no later than the current UTC date. The adapter checks workbook core title
metadata, title cells preceding the holdings header, and explicit fund ticker
fields. A known contradictory fund identity is rejected; absent/ambiguous
identity remains `unverified` and cannot set a positive marker. No actual OIH
workbook body has been received in this work, so whether the real workbook
contains an independent identity field remains unknown. The fund-specific URL
and request slug alone are not body identity; Root technical review is needed
before any live qualification decision.

When a returned workbook body is rejected for identity, the existing rejected-
fetch path retains the complete adapter payload, including base64 original
workbook bytes, raw SHA-256 and byte length, under the existing
`issuer_adapter_rejected_fetch` content-addressed artifact. Its metadata links
the Provider request-log IDs and attempt evidence. The artifact's
`content_hash` is the existing canonical JSON payload hash, distinct from the
raw workbook-byte SHA. The one-shot job latch denies automatic re-fetch. A
redirect response has no workbook body to retain; its Location and Provider
response audit are retained instead.

  records OIH identity 43 with no holdings or candles in the deployed baseline.
  Source code maps OIH to VanEck's `vaneck` adapter and
  `oil-services-etf-oih` workbook slug (`backend/app/services/etf_holdings_adapters.py`);
  deterministic adapter tests exist, but they do not prove current reachability,
  issuer terms, complete live rows, or admission.

  surface only if Root/Provider approve a minimal explicit issuer-only mode.

  fund-ticker identifiers when `sec_cik` is absent, and tries SEC N-PORT/legacy
  fallback when issuer probing/fetch fails. It reuses a bootstrap-ready snapshot

  unless separately reviewed.

  curated VanEck slug, then make one bounded adapter invocation through
  `_refresh_adapter_route` and the existing shared Provider bridge. Count and

  retrieval `known_at`; populate `published_at` only if the workbook establishes

  admin-only and date-specific, not the ordinary user's latest-refresh path.

  tradability checks. Unresolved rows have no guessed ticker/link. Missing
  candles require a second explicit user action delegated to the Provider-owned
  demand API for one canonical instrument, timeframe, and requested/missing
  interval. ETF does not fetch candles; no all-constituent fanout. The Provider

## FHSC3 send-boundary deadline correction — 2026-10-24T16:01Z

Root's review of the in-progress FHSC3 repair found that the worker computed
the SEC attempt timeout before constructing the loop-local transport/client,
then started that duration only after setup. The retained offline probe
`/home/m920q/charting-platform/.ai/staging-attempts/probe-etf-setup-deadline-20261024.py`
reproduced a 0.05-second fund budget with a 0.10-second factory delay: the
physical send began after expiry and was cancelled later. The worker now keeps
the early expiry guard, then recomputes the remaining fund duration after
transport/client/request setup immediately before `client.send`. Expired
setup latches the terminal deadline and performs no send; an in-flight request
still uses the minimum of the existing attempt cap and remaining fund budget,
with timeout settlement behavior unchanged.

Root's follow-up review noted that bare `asyncio.timeout` produces an empty-
message `TimeoutError`, while the DB regression correctly expects a durable
deadline reason. Only when the fund deadline itself expires, the worker now
rethrows `TimeoutError` with the explicit non-secret message `SEC one-fund
execution deadline exceeded`; ordinary attempt timeouts remain unchanged. The
offline real-transport cancellation test asserts that message, preserving the
type used by shared Provider classification.

## Retained RSST against accepted-f04 manual-import contract — read-only — 2026-10-23

Static inspection of exact accepted staging source `0e342512e53ba2268425294d61c50e219eaafa4f`
and the retained `.ai/validation/structural-return-stacked-20261015.{body,headers}`
answers the feasibility question as **not safely importable through accepted f04
yet**. F04 can physically store an explicitly dated artifact, but cannot provide
the complete requested manual-only contract without unsupported identity/profile
workarounds or side effects:

- `ETFHoldingsIngestRequest` accepts `composition_date`, `known_at`, nullable
  `published_at`, `provenance`, `source_provider`, `source_url`, raw payload,
  legal metadata and normalized row fields. It can represent derivatives and
  cash with explicit row/holding types while retaining `raw_payload_text`.
  `legal_metadata.source_tier=none` is recognized by capability classification.
  Do not rely on schema defaults: the schema otherwise defaults quality to
  issuer-current and completeness to complete, neither of which is evidenced
  for this manual sample.
- `ETFHoldingsProfileUpdateRequest` does not accept `adapter_key`. It accepts
  `provider_aliases`, but `ensure_etf_profile` applies `holdings_adapter` only
  when that key exists in the registered ETF adapter catalog. `manual_csv` is
  not registered at f04 (`git grep` found it only as the CSV request's default
  `source_provider`). A direct DB alias/key insert would be an unsupported
  workaround, not a reviewed operator path.
- Both accepted admin ingest routes call the common snapshot ingestion with
  default `allow_provider_enrichment=true`; there is no request field or
  documented manual-only no-enrichment switch. Outside test configuration,
  unresolved rows can reach identifier-provider enrichment. The generic CSV
  parser defaults non-cash rows to `holding_type=equity` and `row_type=security`,
  so it would misclassify the RSST futures. The normalized-row ingest endpoint
  can encode correctly reviewed derivative/cash types, but it does not solve
  enrichment or manual profile binding.
- Accepted-f04 `ingest_holdings_snapshot` always calls `_record_adapter_success`.
  An explicit `source_tier=none` prevents the snapshot from becoming usable for
  current analysis, but the import still writes a successful adapter-health
  row. With an unassigned profile the capability can be `stale`; with a
  concrete profile adapter and tier `none` it is `degraded`. Thus f04 does not
  guarantee the requested clean manual/noncurrent health representation. The
  ETF branch's newer unaccepted safeguard skips that native-success write, but
  is not an accepted-f04 operator contract and does not yet disable enrichment.
- F04 history reads filter explicit point-in-time requests by both
  `composition_date <= requested_date` and `known_at <= end_of_requested_date`
  (or a null `known_at`). The full holdings view offers snapshot-date selection;
  the panel shows a non-current capability notice and only enables opening a
  constituent when capability is current. The basket endpoint rejects an
  unselected non-current request with 409 while an explicit date/snapshot is a
  historical selection. If a later approved import is ever made, it must set a
  non-null `known_at` to the actual import/observation time so an October 15
  query cannot see an artifact imported later; leaving it null would bypass the
  PIT cutoff. `published_at` can remain null. The service's fallback
  `known_at` based on composition date is not suitable for a later import.

## Current issuer-route resilience changes — 2026-09-03

The current working changes extend the committed `15c167e7` checkpoint without
changing the provider-universe split. Beacon's BSR and BTR adapters now follow
the issuer's current Craft-hosted CSV routes and return the resolved holdings
URL from `probe`. The shared issuer-date parser accepts the issuer's `Sept`
spelling, allowing the current Fundsmith ETFT page to remain native without a
locale-specific parser fork. Pictet now accepts the canonical redirected US
product identity and records an AWS WAF challenge when the legacy page returns
the challenge while still validating the public allocation API's symbol-bound

## Tier 0 shadow-gate history and acceptance runbook — 2026-09-04

The ETF canary now retains a bounded 90-observation `canary_history` in each
adapter-state JSON payload. Each observation records timestamp, route status,
capability availability, source/transport tier, identity verification,
symbol-audit outcome, composition/freshness dates, row/completeness/schema
evidence, latency, failure class/streak, circuit state, and recovery. This is
bounded deliberately so daily checks can cover a 30-day production window
without creating an unbounded state payload. The circuit-open path also writes
an observation rather than silently disappearing from the shadow record.

`evaluate_tier0_shadow_gate` provides the machine-readable post-deployment gate:
30 UTC days, at least 95% passing eligible checks, no two consecutive freshness
misses for any Tier 0 symbol, and zero silent identity/schema/completeness
violations. A passing check must be current, identity-verified, complete,
current-analysis-usable, freshness-valid, and backed by issuer-native,
successor-native, or licensed-vendor evidence; successful transport alone is
not sufficient when symbol audit evidence is unresolved. The operational
procedure and escalation rules are documented in `docs/etf-holdings-shadow-gate.md`.

## Schema-drift fail-closed boundary and full validation checkpoint — 2026-09-05

Implementation commit `dd31c80239ca6346b7ad5bfd31e2f11a5a1d1d04`
(`fix(etf): fail closed on schema drift`) hardens the refresh/canary boundary
against unannounced issuer-artifact shape changes. Before any provider-owned
artifact is handed to snapshot ingestion, the refresh route now computes the
same schema fingerprint used by ETF holdings state and compares it with the
persisted adapter fingerprint. A changed fingerprint under the same parser
version raises an explicit `ETFHoldingsSchemaDriftError`, classifies the canary
failure as `schema_drift`, and prevents the snapshot/profile write. The failure
record retains previous and observed fingerprints, parser version, and
observation time for diagnosis and recovery. An explicit parser-version change
is the documented recovery path; a successful refresh clears the prior drift
marker. Lightweight test doubles without a database execute method retain their
existing route-test behavior.

rejected before ingestion, an intentional parser-version change can recover,
and the persisted failure metadata contains comparable fingerprints. Focused
refresh coverage passed `14` tests; the combined refresh/capability/resolution
suite passed `114`; the deterministic adapter suite passed `571`; and the
complete ETF API integration suite passed `66` with two existing warnings.

The capability-canary runner now applies an explicit per-symbol timeout budget
through `ETF_HOLDINGS_CAPABILITY_CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default `60`). A
timed-out adapter refresh is recorded as a transport failure and flows through
the existing failure streak, circuit, capability, and persisted canary-history
paths instead of allowing one issuer route to hold the entire sweep open.
The timeout is configurable for deployment environments with different route
latency constraints; it does not alter adapter parsing, source eligibility, or
the shared provider-platform governance boundary.

### Branch-owned failures resolved — 2026-10-07

The final full integration gate passed after moving both functional and visual
Playwright runs into the pinned Playwright 1.62.1 container on the ETF stack's
private Compose network (`http://frontend`). This avoids host-loopback
network-change failures by routing browser traffic over the same Compose

application cause: `crypto.randomUUID()` is unavailable on insecure HTTP
origins, and the Chart Template and Virtual Watchlist key generators called it
without a fallback. Both now use a random-string fallback; a component test
explicitly removes `crypto.randomUUID` and verifies template persistence. The
affected E2E cases now pass on the real app stack.

### Provider egress and Playwright boundary

The outer process sets `RUN_LIVE_PROVIDER_TESTS=0` and
`RUN_LIVE_ETF_HOLDINGS_TESTS=0` explicitly; dotenv must not override these
values. `scripts/run-live-provider-probes.py` should print its disabled result,
which is not live-provider acceptance. The normal deterministic mocks and
shared-runtime positive/negative tests remain enabled. No issuer, SEC, provider
or quota request is permitted.

The full-stack Compose overlay is the egress boundary: `charting` is an
internal network; backend and worker have `PROVIDER_ROUTING_ENABLED=false` and
HTTP(S)/ALL proxy variables pointing to `provider-egress-deny`, whose every
HTTP method and CONNECT returns 403 while logging only hostname. The only
service attached to `host-access` is `host-port-relay`; it forwards only to the
project frontend and backend fixed destinations and receives no provider
credentials. The Playwright container joins only `<stack>_charting`, uses
`STACK_URL=http://frontend`, and can reach only the local app network; it has
no external-provider route. `make test-compose-contract` must verify this
shape before stack startup. Dependency/image registry access by host-side
locked installs/builds is separate from runtime market-data egress.

The locked frontend package resolves Playwright/Test at `1.62.1`; use the
verified Noble image digest above and Chromium preinstalled in that image, not
host Chromium. At launch capture the output of `fc-match 'DejaVu Sans'` and
`fc-match 'Liberation Sans'`, the resolved font-file paths, and
fontconfig/package versions inside the exact pinned image. Do not
install/change fonts, regenerate snapshots, normalize baselines, change masks,
or alter visual assertions. All visual references, 0.005 `maxDiffPixelRatio`,
and zero retries remain exact.

The repository Make target sets `CI=1`, while current Playwright config maps
that to one retry. The coordinator requires zero browser retries. To satisfy
both without editing tracked config or tests, root must review a temporary
`PLAYWRIGHT_DOCKER` launcher override that mirrors the Makefile's existing
container arguments and appends CLI `--retries=0` to both Playwright commands.
It must preserve `CI=1` (`forbidOnly` and `failOnFlakyTests` remain active),
workers=1, the internal stack network, host UID mapping, workspace mount,
`STACK_URL=http://frontend`, E2E seed flags, and the pinned image digest. If
the coordinator does not approve this exact override or it cannot be verified
to apply to both the functional and visual invocations, do not launch the
profile; do not change Playwright config as a workaround.

Reviewed launcher contract (create only after root approval):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
exec docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --userns=host \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  --network "${STACK_COMPOSE_PROJECT}_charting" \
  -v "$(pwd):/workspace" -w /workspace/frontend \
  -e STACK_URL=http://frontend -e E2E_SEED_MARKET_DATA \
  -e RUN_BOARD_VISUAL_PARITY -e PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS -e CI \
  mcr.microsoft.com/playwright@sha256:dcc5531e97840b9b5e794f2814476b21571c5124a3fca2267d73041f56e7580e \
  "$@" --retries=0
```

The make command-line variable `PLAYWRIGHT_DOCKER` would point to this
temporary launcher, so both existing invocations (`npx playwright test` and
the strict visual-spec invocation) receive the same zero-retry override. The
wrapper's final generated argv must be inspected in dry-run form before
launch; no container is started by that review.

exist:

ETF_PROFILE_RUN_ID=etf-full-profile-bbf57daf-20261021 \

## FHSC3 uvloop timer-cause correction — 2026-10-24

Root released the source freeze for this narrow production cause fix. Exact
published CI `40114130605` on `39c411b910fcac5c637163cffd13ae68286988f4` is
terminal RED: Backend unit result `5429 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped` in
`676.90s`; Frontend passed and downstream jobs were skipped. The sole failing
test was `test_sec_worker_cancels_real_httpx_transport_at_remaining_fund_deadline`.
Its real HTTPX transport was cancelled by asyncio's fund-selected timer under
uvloop, but a subsequent strict read of the SEC budget clock still returned
just before the fund deadline. The handler consequently failed to latch the
fund terminal reason and rethrew a bare `TimeoutError`. This exact CI failure
is preserved, not retried or called green.

The production correction carries the selected per-attempt timeout and a
fund-bound flag from one budget-clock read into the actual `asyncio.timeout`
scope. A caught `TimeoutError` becomes terminal fund expiry only when that
scope reports `expired()` and the selected timeout came from the fund bound;
equal fund/attempt bounds deliberately count as fund-bound. Attempt-cap-only
timeouts and a transport-raised timeout before the timer fires remain

Provider's exact review of candidate a3a90ae1964f88ab01b624e06f7a1a2122831770
identified two real bridge gaps: disabled policy was rejected before the sealed
initial VanEck context could be considered, and Provider request-log IDs were
durable only for SEC qualification jobs. The repair is source commit
7157269abced8fc975f9dffd9441b81c11ebed08, limited to the ETF bridge,
qualification/refresh pass-through, and focused ETF tests. It does not change
Provider-owned source. The disabled-policy pre-review now opens only for the
current Provider-sealed authority bound to the exact committed running OIH
job, profile/instrument/symbol, VanEck capability/operation, account scope,
review revision, unexpired URL/host, and empty prior request-ID list. Ordinary
disabled routes still stop before transport; Provider's global stop, free-only,
entitlement, host, account, holds, quota reservation/settlement and execution
checks remain required.

The shared runtime's independent transaction now links only its exact settled
VanEck request logs to that same active job and scope; the SEC linkage path is
unchanged. Qualification verifies the durable provider log and content-addressed
raw workbook, with the raw artifact bound to the internal ETF holdings data
source used by snapshot ingestion and its separate VanEck source metadata. The
failure finalizer uses a scalar job ID captured before commit/rollback, avoiding
